_purpose: #3374 R1 — the committed cost-bearing-surface baseline. HAND-OWNED, deliberately NOT written by scripts/generate_platform_model.py: the generator derives the live counts into model/platform_model.json's cost_surface plane, and tests/test_platform_model_drift.py exact-pins this file against them. A PR that grows a cost-bearing population (a new schedule, alarm, EMF namespace, secret, or budget-guard AI feature) must bump the matching count HERE, in the same diff — that hand edit is the ratchet's deliberate act. A shrink must ratchet the count down the same way, so the baseline can never rot above the estate.
_last_change: #3764 (2026-09-13): schedules 88 -> 89 and alarms 125 -> 126 — a daily EventBridge rule on the EXISTING hevy-backfill function that republishes config/hevy_template_index.json from the live Hevy catalogue, plus the dead-man that watches it (hevy-template-index-not-rebuilt-48h). No new Lambda and no new invocation cost of consequence (one extra invoke/day of a 256MB function, plus ~9 Hevy GETs); the index had no producer at all since it was hand-built on 2026-06-01, and had drifted 789 indexed vs 828 live. The alarm is a standard CloudWatch metric alarm (~$0.10/mo) watching a single custom metric in the existing LifePlatform/HevyRoutine namespace — no new EMF namespace. It is the only thing that can see this job die: the rebuild swallows all three of its failure modes, so nothing raises, and the hourly poll on the same function keeps Invocations green regardless.
